title: Community Concealment from Graph Neural Networks
abstract: arXiv:2602.12250v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs) enable powerful unsupervised learning of communities. However, such inference may inadvertently expose sensitive group structures, critical clustered patterns, or collective behaviors, raising concerns about sensitive group-level privacy. In social and critical infrastructure networks, unauthorized community inference can reveal coordinated asset groups, operational hierarchies, and system dependencies that may be exploited for reconnaissance or profiling. We study a defensive setting in which a network (or defender) operator seeks to conceal a community of interest while making only small, utility-preserving modifications to the network. Our analysis shows that community concealment depends on two measurable factors: the connectivity at the community boundary and the feature similarity between the protected community and its neighbors. translated_title: 从图神经网络中隐藏社区
translated_abstract: 图神经网络（GNNs）实现了强大的无监督社区学习。然而，这种推理可能无意中暴露敏感群体结构、关键聚类模式或集体行为，引发对敏感群体级隐私的担忧。在社交和关键基础设施网络中，未经授权的社区推理可能揭示协调的资产群体、运营层级和系统依赖关系，这些信息可能被利用进行侦察或画像分析。我们研究了一种防御性设置，其中网络（或防御者）操作者旨在隐藏感兴趣的社区，同时仅对网络进行小而保持效用的修改。我们的分析表明，社区隐藏依赖于两个可测量的因素：社区边界的连通性以及受保护社区与其邻居之间的特征相似性。在这些观察的指导下，我们引入了特征-社区引导的D（模型或方法名称，原文截断）。
tldr: 本文提出了一种基于社区边界连通性和特征相似性的方法，通过最小化网络修改来防御图神经网络对敏感社区的推理攻击。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a method based on community boundary connectivity and feature similarity to defend against GNN-based inference of sensitive communities via minimal network modifications.
